base_result: R50G20 proved that a complete frozen RUP pass from an R33-fixed six-variable width6 entry cannot end nonterminal at width6; any unsafe V7 descendant was reduced to V6/W5 or safe, while preserving the ancestry firewall between DIRECT5 and RUP6-descended W5.
target_theorems: Let H0 be the R33/BCE-fixed six-variable RUP-entry state, R=(sigma*z OR C) a full width6 clause, z the minimum variable selected by frozen lit_key, and C=R without the z literal. If C is not already present in H0, then a width5 C created by RUP6 collapse cannot survive unchanged to the complete RUP fixpoint.

PROPER_Z_WITNESS_CASE: if some nonblocking opposite-z witness D=(-sigma*z OR S) has S proper subset of C, choose l in C\S; after R is strengthened to C, BCE witnesses for R on l plus D give a persistent UP conflict certifying C\{l}.

TWIN_CASE: if every nonblocking opposite-z witness has full support C, H0 contains the opposite full twin T=(-sigma*z OR C). BCE fixedness of both R and T gives opposite-z support witnesses for every l in C; after C is created, assumptions negating C\{l} force l and then either conflict directly or force both z polarities. Hence C\{l} is RUP-valid.

LAST_CREATION: if C was absent at H0, finitely many width6 clauses may recreate C by dedup/collapse, but after the last creation the persistent deletion certificate remains; therefore C cannot be present at the nonterminal RUP fixpoint.

FINAL_W5_PROVENANCE: RUP never widens, so every width5 clause at the nonterminal RUP fixpoint was already width5 at H0. In the R50G14 V7 unsafe ancestry bifurcation, surviving W5 ancestry therefore cannot be RUP6_DROP_HUB and must be DIRECT5.
